A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HGP research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The expanded evaluation and reorganized supplement in v4 can be matched reliably to v2.

before.justification: v2 reports original HGP benchmark results, bias analyses, component ablations, and feature-inversion examples. Its attribution of several baseline results to prior work does not affect this judgment.

after.justification: v4 reports original results across six classification benchmarks, component ablations, and a new 100-client participation study, alongside retained empirical analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain shared prefix prompting, weighted aggregation, hierarchical Gaussian-mixture sampling, and classifier rebalancing. v4 newly specifies diagonal covariance and makes its appendix consistent with the single prompt already proposed in v2's main text. These disclosures do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The benchmark suite changes from CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet to CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, EuroSAT, Cars-196, and CUB-200, substantially broadening domain and task coverage. Tiny-ImageNet remains in the retained privacy reconstruction example, although its benchmark evaluation is removed.

E2.justification: The comparison suite adds FisherAVG, RegMean, DualPrompt, FedProto, PIP, and LoRM, while removing iCaRL, GLFC, and LGA. These changes are reflected in reported comparisons. PLoRA in v2 and PILoRA in v4 refer to the same Guo et al. work and are matched as a retained comparator.

E3.justification: v4 drops quantity-based partitions and AIA evaluation. Reported HGP prompt-component shape changes from (8,768) to (200,768), local batch size from 64 to 16, and the CIFAR-100 learning rate from 0.001 to 0.003. It adds 100-client experiments with varying participation. Exact settings for some new results remain ambiguous: Table 2's EuroSAT/Cars-196 beta headings conflict with Section 4.1 and Appendices G–H.

E4.justification: v4 adds sensitivity analysis for participation rates with 100 clients and revises the component ablation to cover CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and CUB-200. It removes v2 Appendix C's investigation of L2P with versus without batch-wise prompting. The prompting-versus-fine-tuning analysis and privacy reconstruction case are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three runs. v4 explicitly identifies different seeds and adds standard deviations for the principal benchmark comparisons in Appendix G, Tables A–B. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in run count.

E6.justification: The main results are extensively replaced and expanded, while Tiny-ImageNet benchmark scores and AIA entries disappear. For example, CIFAR-100 beta=0.05 HGP FAA changes from 89.0 to 90.16 alongside revised training settings, so this is not an isolated same-setting gain. New results include the participation study and LoRM outperforming HGP in two Cars-196 columns of Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the JSD/GMM reasoning remain unchanged. New Appendix B adds limited analytical cost reasoning for hierarchical sampling, including O(1) categorical draws, O(feature dimension) Gaussian sampling, and an approximately 770-FLOP estimate.

C1.justification: The central contribution—localizing bias through prompting and mitigating it through hierarchical generative rebalancing—is retained. The abstract removes the specific +7.8% average accuracy claim and instead states performance across six datasets with three scenarios each. The conclusion shifts emphasis toward learnable-parameter efficiency.

C2.justification: v4 replaces the general interpretation that old-class rebalancing is more important with a dataset-dependent account emphasizing CUB-200. It adds explanations involving class count and low-rank adaptation, scalability interpretations, and a limitation concerning malicious clients. The new Appendix E claim of outperforming every comparator at 10% participation is not supported by Table 1's PIP and LoRM scores.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds extensive per-dataset, per-method hyperparameter tables. v4 also discloses diagonal covariance, Alias sampling, and computational-cost estimates, and revises documented prompt and training settings. Its appendix resolves v2's inconsistent prompt-pool description. The code-in-supplement availability statement from v2's abstract is removed; this does not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v4 adds references and positioning for model merging, PIP, and LoRM, together with citations for the new benchmarks and Alias sampling. The existing FL/CIL/FCIL related-work framework largely remains intact. The renamed and updated PLoRA/PILoRA citation represents the same prior work.

P1.justification: The experimental setup, comparison narrative, and component discussion are substantially rewritten. The two ablation subsections reverse order, and the supplement is reorganized around additional topics with implementation details and the algorithm relocated. Much of the introduction and methodology wording remains stable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Main tables are rebuilt into grouped multi-dataset FAA displays, with second-best underlining. The communication display changes from a logarithmic scatter plot plus directional-cost table to three linear-axis plots. Standard-deviation and hyperparameter tables are added, while the batch-wise prompting table is removed.

improvement.justification: Broader benchmark coverage, updated comparisons, standard deviations, and detailed hyperparameters provide a useful net gain in validation and reproducibility. The gain is limited by removing AIA and the L2P testing audit, conflicting beta labels in Table 2 versus Section 4.1 and Appendices G–H, and an overstated scalability conclusion: Appendix E's 80.82% does not exceed Table 1's PIP 81.40% or LoRM 82.76%.
